I found 19 households to call. Five have a partly taxable backdoor Roth, ten have an unmet 2025 RMD, and four have a wash sale. None were left unresolved. I worked only from the files, as they stood on 15 April 2026.

**Backdoor Roth partly taxable (5 households).** Each person put a nondeductible 2025 contribution into a new traditional IRA and converted it. The pro-rata rule pulls in every traditional IRA the person owns, and each also had a rollover IRA holding pre-tax money on 31 Dec 2025. Their recorded IRA basis was $0, so the taxable part is the conversion × (1 − contribution ÷ (31 Dec rollover IRA balance + conversion)):

| Household | Person | Conversion | Rollover IRA on 31 Dec 2025 | Taxable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0690 | Nadia Brannigan | $8,000 (T-0690-0006) | $187,878.56 | ≈ $7,673.27 |
| HH-0218 | Yusuf Rasmussen | $7,000 (T-0218-0006) | $221,659.62 | ≈ $6,785.71 |
| HH-0347 | Hana Yamaguchi | $7,000 (T-0347-0006) | $231,265.99 | ≈ $6,794.35 |
| HH-0844 | Anders Moreau | $7,000 (T-0844-0006) | $152,329.55 | ≈ $6,692.46 |
| HH-1204 | Luka Kovac | $7,000 (T-1204-0006) | $187,544.92 | ≈ $6,748.13 |

Five other backdoor Roths are clean (HH-0799, 1587, 0633, 0608, 0747). Their pre-tax money is in a 401(k), which doesn't count, and the new IRA was empty at year-end.

**2025 RMD not met (10 households).**
- **401(k) never paid (5 households).** Each owner signed one combined RMD payment from an IRA that included the 401(k)'s share. An IRA payment can't meet a 401(k)'s RMD. Each owner was born in 1952, so this was their first RMD year and the deadline was 1 April 2026, which has already passed. The 401(k) shortfalls (31 Dec 2024 balance ÷ 26.5):
  - HH-0120, Laila Udeh: SYN-01200004, $12,582.44
  - HH-5271, Teodoro Villanueva: SYN-52710004, $12,729.96
  - HH-0664, Freya Chaudhry: SYN-06640004, $11,019.74
  - HH-0236, Xavier Santangelo: SYN-02360004, $10,955.88
  - HH-0371, Rosa Tamura: SYN-03710004, $15,164.26
- **Inherited IRAs with nothing paid out (5 households).** The CRM says each parent had already begun RMDs before dying. That means the child beneficiary owes yearly RMDs under the ten-year rule, and 2025 was due by 31 Dec 2025. Nothing was paid in 2025 from any of them:
  - HH-0607, Noor: SYN-06070002
  - HH-0466, Zainab: SYN-04660002
  - HH-0842, Ines: SYN-08420002
  - HH-7126, Samuel: SYN-71260002
  - HH-0491, Orla: SYN-04910002

  I didn't calculate these amounts. They need the IRS Single Life Table, which isn't in the files.

**Wash sales (4 households).** In each, a joint taxable account sold at a loss and the spouse's IRA bought the same fund within 30 days. Because the replacement is inside an IRA, the disallowed part of the loss is lost for good.

| Household | Loss sale | Replacement | Disallowed / allowed |

| HH-0129 | 642 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 3 Oct, loss $31,896.36 (T-0129-0035) | 360 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 15 Oct, Jun's Roth IRA (T-0129-0037) | $17,885.81 / $14,010.55 |
| HH-9234 | 847 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 3 Nov, loss $53,516.17 (T-9234-0035) | 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 19 Nov, Ingrid's IRA (T-9234-0037) | $31,591.60 / $21,924.57 |

Seven other 2025 losses had their repurchase or RSU vest outside the window:
- On the 31st day: HH-9571 and HH-0679.
- 35 to 55 days away: HH-0380, HH-0847, HH-0981, HH-0420 and HH-0514.

**Two things outside the three kinds, not counted:**
- **HH-3058:** the custodian recorded $0 basis on the Bramwell Devices Group shares Priya sold. Using the vest values in the CRM, both lots were gains, so it isn't a wash sale, but the custodian's reported gain is overstated.
- **HH-0782:** the custodian recorded Felix's $7,500 charitable gift from his IRA as an ordinary distribution. The CRM has the charity's receipt. His RMD was met either way.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households should we call before 15 April 2026 about a 2025 tax or distribution surprise, and why?

Count three kinds of surprise, and no other:
- "backdoor_roth_taxed": a 2025 contribution to a traditional IRA converted to a Roth IRA in 2025, part of which is taxable under the pro-rata rule because the person's traditional IRAs held pre-tax money on 31 December 2025;
- "rmd_not_met": a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any retirement account, that was not met;
- "wash_sale": a 2025 sale at a loss in a taxable account, with the same security acquired within 30 days before or after it in an account of the seller or the seller's spouse, so that some of the loss is a wash sale.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households had such a surprise, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household to call, each as {"household_id": ..., "surprises": the kinds above that apply, "person_ids": the person each surprise concerns (who converted, whose RMD was not met), "account_ids": the accounts an unmet RMD had to come from, "transaction_ids": the backdoor Roth's conversion, and the wash sale's loss sales and the acquisitions that replace them, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
